newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 15.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- A woman was killed, three others injured and more than 400 families of people evacuated when a dam-shaped concrete wall collapsed on Wednesday at an apartment complex in northern Seoul.
- Prosecutors today will summon Kim Hyun-chul, the second son of President Kim Young-sam, to question him on graft and influence-peddling, prosecutor officials said.

- Opposition leader Kim Jong-pil hinted that he may run in the presidential election in December even if his candidacy undermines the opposition's joint effort to field a unified presidential candidate.
- Korea's economic growth is expected to fall behind that of the United States for the first time in 31 years, this year.
- An international consortium for supplying light-water reactors to North Korea agreed on Tuesday to start building the infrastructure for the reactors from the middle of July.

- North Korea, apparently unable to feed its people, poses the greatest threat to peace in Asia, Gen. John Shalikashvili, chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff, told Chinese army officials on Wednesday.
